ledger.x: 396 BC: the Boii 'settled south of the Po, between the river and the Apennines' 'from about the early 4th century BC'; 'Diodorus and Pliny date the start to 396 BC'; the Etruscan page: 'from 396 BC: Invasion of the Celts into the Po Valley'.
295 BC: Sentinum, with the Senones, Samnites and Etruscans.
284-283 BC: 'Lake Vadimon: 284 BC' with the Etruscans and Senones.
283 BC: Roman victory; the Senones subjugated.
225 BC: the Gallic war; the Boii fight at Telamon (225) with the Insubres and Gaesatae.
225 BC: Telamon; 'After Telamon the Boii made their first formal submission to Rome by treaty', so the Boian contest ends here (the war went on against the Insubres to 222, see insubres).
225 BC: after Telamon the Boii submit to Rome by treaty ('their first formal submission'); the land is tinted from roman-republic (vassal_start boii 225).
218-191 BC: the Hannibalic rising and reconquest.
218 BC (November): on Hannibal's arrival, 'before the Battle of the Trebia, they concluded an alliance with him'; the treaty tie of 225 ends (roman-republic vassal_end boii 218, month 11).
218 BC: the Boii leave the Roman sphere with Hannibal's alliance; the Boian land is Roman-tinted no more (mirror of roman-republic's loss to the Boii in November 218).
191 BC: 'Resistance ended around 191 BC with Scipio Nasica's victory'; Rome took 'only about half their territory' (Williams), Bononia founded 189 'on the site of Felsina', Parma and Mutina 183.
191 BC: conquest; 'Scipio Nasica completed the conquest of the Boii'.

wars.name: Gallic war of 225-222 BC
wars.outcome: Roman victory: Telamon 225, Clastidium and Mediolanum 222

wars.name: Boian war of the Second Punic War and the reconquest
wars.outcome: Boii allied with Hannibal (218), Silva Litana (216), reconquest from 201, conquest 191

certainty.note: Emilia between the Po and the Apennines; the Lingones to the east and the Anares to the west are folded in.
